descriptors.concept_name: Impairment losses recognised or reversed in the period
descriptors.definition: An entity must disclose specific details for each material impairment loss or reversal recognized during the period for individual assets or cash-generating units. Required disclosures include underlying events, financial amounts, asset classification, and fair value hierarchy levels or valuation techniques.
inclusion: events leading to recognition or reversal
amount of impairment loss or reversal
nature and segment of individual assets
description and class breakdown of cash-generating units
valuation hierarchy levels and key assumptions for fair value less costs of disposal
exclusion: general unallocated corporate assets lacking specific impairment events
nearby_distinctions: Unlike aggregate disclosures for minor losses, this node mandates granular reporting for individually material impairment events.

descriptors.concept_name: Other impairment losses/reversals material in aggregate to the financial statements
descriptors.definition: When individual impairment losses or reversals are not material on a standalone basis, an entity must disclose aggregate figures if they are material collectively. This includes identifying the primary asset classes affected and the principal economic events driving these aggregate adjustments.
inclusion: aggregate impairment losses for the period
aggregate impairment reversals for the period
main classes of affected assets
main events and circumstances causing the losses and reversals
exclusion: material individual impairment losses reported separately
immaterial items not qualifying as material in aggregate
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from itemized disclosures of material individual losses by focusing strictly on pooled figures that become significant only when combined.

descriptors.definition: If a portion of goodwill acquired in a business combination remains unallocated to any cash-generating unit at the end of the reporting period, the entity must disclose that specific amount. Additionally, the entity is required to provide clear reasons explaining why the goodwill allocation has not yet been completed.
inclusion: monetary amount of unallocated goodwill at period end
justifications explaining why the goodwill amount remains unallocated
exclusion: goodwill successfully allocated to specific cash-generating units or groups of units
nearby_distinctions: Differs from allocated goodwill disclosures because it addresses acquisition synergies that have not yet been successfully assigned to operating cash-generating units.

descriptors.concept_name: Information to be disclosed for CGUs to which significant goodwill or indefinite – life intangible assets have been allocated
descriptors.definition: Entities holding cash-generating units with significant allocations of goodwill or indefinite-life intangibles must disclose detailed valuation inputs. This includes the basis of recoverable amount determination, growth rates, projection periods, and applied discount rates.
inclusion: carrying amount of allocated goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles
basis of recoverable amount determination
management's key assumptions and projection approaches
forecast periods exceeding five years with justifications
growth rates and discount rates applied to cash flows
exclusion: cash-generating units where goodwill or indefinite-life intangibles are insignificant in comparison to total carrying amounts
nearby_distinctions: Applies strictly to units with significant carrying amounts of goodwill or indefinite-life intangibles, separating them from minor allocations.

descriptors.concept_name: Information to be disclosed for CGUs to which insignificant goodwill or indefinite-life intangible assets have been allocated
descriptors.definition: When goodwill or indefinite-life intangibles are allocated across multiple units where each allocation is insignificant individually but significant in aggregate, specific disclosures are required. Entities must disclose the aggregate carrying amounts, shared key assumptions, and sensitivity details if reasonably possible changes would eliminate the headroom.
inclusion: aggregate carrying amounts of insignificant allocations
description of shared key assumptions and management approaches
excess of recoverable amount over carrying amount when sensitive
required change in key assumptions to trigger impairment
exclusion: individually significant goodwill or indefinite-life intangible allocations
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on pooled insignificant units that share common key assumptions, contrasting with standalone reporting for individually large units.

descriptors.concept_name: EXTRACTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF LISTED ENTITY
descriptors.definition: This section provides practical illustrations and comparative standard overviews regarding impairment accounting policies applied by listed entities. It serves as a structural transition into comparing Indian Accounting Standards with predecessor accounting rules.
inclusion: annual report references for impairment policies
comparative framework tables highlighting differences between Ind AS and AS
exclusion: hypothetical numerical exercises not drawn from actual financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Acts as an empirical application guide preceding technical standard comparisons rather than containing isolated theoretical rules.

descriptors.concept_name: SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES IN IND AS 36 VIS-À-VIS AS 28
descriptors.definition: This comparative framework details the structural and technical divergences between Ind AS 36 and AS 28 regarding asset scope, annual testing rules, and goodwill reversals. Major differences include mandatory annual testing for goodwill under Ind AS and differing treatments for goodwill impairment reversals.
inclusion: inclusion of specific financial assets and exclusion of biological assets under Ind AS 36
mandatory annual impairment testing for indefinite-life intangibles and goodwill
prohibition of goodwill impairment reversals under Ind AS 36 versus allowance under AS 28
differences in bottom-up and top-down allocation approaches
exclusion: harmonized rules where Ind AS 36 and AS 28 maintain identical provisions without divergence
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts modern global convergence accounting treatments with legacy local accounting standards for asset impairment.
